document.title: NuSCR Software Requirements Specification - Notional Four-Channel Reactor Protection System (Bistable Processor and Coincidence Processor)
document.status: SYNTHETIC REFERENCE SPECIFICATION - NOT DERIVED FROM ANY PLANT DESIGN - NOT FOR OPERATIONAL, LICENSING OR SAFETY-CLASSIFIED USE WITHOUT FULL INDEPENDENT V&V
document.provenance: Generated by tools/build_spec.py.  The specification uses the NuSCR notation (FOD, SDT, FSM, TTS; f_/h_/th_/k_/g_ naming) and groups the trip functions into four logic categories (fixed set-point, variable set-point, manual reset and digital trips).  The set of trip functions is modelled at a general level on publicly described pressurized-water-reactor protection systems.  The design is notional and is not derived from any existing plant specification; every logic detail, constant, setpoint, delay and range is an illustrative choice.
limitations: All constants (setpoints, hysteresis, delays, ranges, rates) are ILLUSTRATIVE placeholders. Real values must come from the plant safety analysis and an approved setpoint methodology (e.g. ISA-67.04.01 / NRC RG 1.105).
The logic is a notional design. It has not been reviewed against any plant's system requirements, safety analysis, hazard analysis or regulatory requirements.

The specification has been checked for internal consistency by the tools in this package (SDT completeness/disjointness, FSM/TTS determinism, invariant and obligation proofs, simulation tests). This is not a substitute for independent verification and validation (e.g. IEEE 1012, IEC 60880, IEEE 7-4.3.2) under a nuclear quality-assurance programme.
Hardware, input conditioning, communication protocols, manual trip, reactor trip switchgear and the engineered safety features actuation system are outside the scope of this specification.

semantics.execution: Each module executes synchronously in scan cycles of period k_Scan_Period.  At the start of a cycle all inputs are sampled.  Nodes are then evaluated once, in the module's execution_order (a topological order of the FOD data flow with ties broken by FOD node number).  A node reads the current-cycle value of every other variable it references.  An FSM/TTS reading its own variable reads the value from the previous cycle.
semantics.sdt: A Structured Decision Table defines a function variable (stateless).  Each rule (column) is the conjunction of its condition cells (T = condition holds, F = condition does not hold, - = don't care).  In every cycle exactly one rule must hold (completeness and disjointness are proved by nuscr_check.py), and the variable takes the value of that rule's action.
semantics.fsm: A Finite State Machine defines a history variable.  In each cycle, the transitions leaving the current state are evaluated; guards leaving a state are pairwise disjoint (proved), so at most one is enabled.  If one is enabled it is taken, its action becomes the variable's new value and the target state becomes current.  If none is enabled the state and value are unchanged.  At most one transition is taken per cycle.
semantics.tts: A Timed Transition System defines a timed-history variable.  It behaves like an FSM, except that a transition labelled [lower, upper] is enabled only when its guard holds and the time spent in the source state, tau = (current cycle - entry cycle) * k_Scan_Period, satisfies lower <= tau <= upper.  Every timed guard is required (and proved) to be complemented by the untimed exits of its source state, so the guard holds continuously for the whole time spent in that state: the timed transition therefore fires after the condition has persisted for 'lower'.
semantics.initialization: Before the first cycle every history and timed-history variable is set to its initial_value and its machine to its initial_state; the initial state counts as entered one cycle before the first scan.  Function variables have no initial value.
semantics.types: Finite types enumerate their admissible values; inputs of finite type are assumed to be restricted to those values by input conditioning (the simulator rejects anything else).  Type 'real' is an exact rational/real quantity; analog inputs are NOT assumed to lie in any range (validity is checked by SDTs).
semantics.ranges: A 'range' on a computed variable is an invariant.  nuscr_check.py proves it inductively (initial value and every rule/transition preserve it, assuming the proved ranges of the variables read) and then uses it as an assumption in all other proofs.

conventions.polarity: Trip and pre-trip signals are de-energize-to-trip: 0 = TRIP / PRETRIP, 1 = NORMAL.  Error flags: 1 = error.  Validity flags: 1 = valid.

requirements.text: Each RPS channel shall execute its protection logic cyclically with a fixed scan period k_Scan_Period; inputs are sampled once at the start of each scan.
allocated_to: Execution semantics of every module (semantics.execution) with scan period k_Scan_Period

requirements.text: A trip function shall be placed in the tripped state, and its pre-trip alarm actuated, without intentional delay whenever an error of the function is present. The errors of a function are: a processor module error (f_Module_Error = 1), a channel error (f_Channel_Error = 1), an invalid process input of the function, and for functions using core protection calculator signals the loss of the CPC data link.  An input used only by an operating-bypass permissive is not a process input: while it is invalid the permissive is not satisfied (SYS-GEN-09).
Each analog process input f_S shall be declared invalid when it lies outside its valid range [k_S_Valid_Min, k_S_Valid_Max].

At start-up every trip and pre-trip output shall be in the tripped state and every operating bypass shall be removed; an output shall leave the tripped state only in a scan in which no error of the function is present.  When an error that did not interrupt a process trip clears (or at start-up) while the trip (pre-trip) condition is present and the function is not in operating bypass, the output shall remain tripped; it shall become a process trip if the condition persists for the trip (pre-trip) delay, and shall return to NORMAL as soon as the condition clears.  A process trip interrupted by an error is governed by SYS-GEN-07.
Trip and pre-trip outputs shall use de-energize-to-trip polarity: 0 = TRIP/PRETRIP, 1 = NORMAL.

A trip (pre-trip) caused by a process condition shall be generated when, and only when, the condition has persisted continuously for the trip (pre-trip) delay of the function.  Process conditions are evaluated only in scans in which no error of the function is present; persistence is measured over consecutive such scans in which the function is not in operating bypass, so an error or an active operating bypass interrupts it.  When a bypass is removed while the condition is present, the trip follows after the delay.

Once tripped (pre-tripped) by a process condition, a trip function shall remain tripped until the process variable has recovered past the trip (pre-trip) setpoint by more than the reset hysteresis, or the function is placed in operating bypass.  A process trip is held through errors of the function; its release condition is evaluated only in scans without an error of the function.
Each trip function shall provide a pre-trip alarm generated at a setpoint closer to normal operating conditions than the trip setpoint.

An operating bypass shall be established only by an operator initiation, i.e. a press of its initiation pushbutton made while its permissive condition is satisfied; a pushbutton held or stuck in the pressed state (including at start-up) shall not establish a bypass.  A permissive is not satisfied while its input is invalid.  The bypass shall be removed automatically, without operator action, in the first scan in which the permissive is no longer satisfied.  While bypassed, the function's process trip and pre-trip are inhibited; trips caused by errors are not inhibited.
The status of each trip channel bypass switch shall be transmitted with the channel's trip outputs to the coincidence processors.
For each trip function the coincidence processor shall generate a coincidence trip when at least two of the four channels are tripped (2-out-of-4).

A channel with a trip channel bypass requested shall be excluded from the vote of that function (2-out-of-3 logic), provided no other channel requests bypass of the same function; if two or more channels request bypass of the same function, all those requests shall be ignored (2-out-of-4 logic retained).
A channel whose data link has failed shall be counted as tripped for every trip function for which it is not validly bypassed.
The coincidence processor shall generate the reactor trip initiation signal when the coincidence trip of any trip function is present.

The RPS shall generate a Variable Overpower trip when the excore linear nuclear power (f_NPWR_LIN) rises to or above the variable trip setpoint h_VOPT_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above h_VOPT_Trip_SP - k_VOPT_Pretrip_Margin.

The trip setpoint h_VOPT_Trip_SP shall track f_NPWR_LIN + k_VOPT_Band limited to [k_VOPT_SP_Min, k_VOPT_SP_Max].  It shall follow decreasing power without delay and shall increase at no more than k_VOPT_SP_Rate, so that a rapid power increase produces a trip.  At start-up it shall be initialised from the first valid input.

The RPS shall generate a High Logarithmic Power Level trip when the excore logarithmic nuclear power (f_NPWR_LOG) rises to or above k_LOGP_HI_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above k_LOGP_HI_Pretrip_SP.
The High Logarithmic Power Level trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_LOGP_HI_OB_Ini) while f_NPWR_LOG >= k_LOGP_HI_OB_Perm.

The RPS shall generate a High Local Power Density (CPC) trip when the core protection calculator reports a local power density trip (f_LPD_HI_Trip_In = 0), and a pre-trip alarm when it reports a pre-trip (f_LPD_HI_Pretrip_In = 0).  Loss of the CPC data link (f_CPC_Link_Error = 1) shall be treated as an error.
The High Local Power Density (CPC) trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_LPD_HI_OB_Ini) while the low-power permissive is present (f_NPWR_LOG < k_LP_OB_Perm).

The RPS shall generate a Low DNBR (CPC) trip when the core protection calculator reports a departure from nucleate boiling ratio trip (f_DNBR_LO_Trip_In = 0), and a pre-trip alarm when it reports a pre-trip (f_DNBR_LO_Pretrip_In = 0).  Loss of the CPC data link (f_CPC_Link_Error = 1) shall be treated as an error.
The Low DNBR (CPC) trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_DNBR_LO_OB_Ini) while the low-power permissive is present (f_NPWR_LOG < k_LP_OB_Perm).

The RPS shall generate a High Pressurizer Pressure trip when the pressurizer pressure (wide range) (f_PZR_P) rises to or above k_PZR_P_HI_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above k_PZR_P_HI_Pretrip_SP.

The RPS shall generate a Low Pressurizer Pressure trip when the pressurizer pressure (wide range) (f_PZR_P) falls to or below the variable trip setpoint h_PZR_P_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below h_PZR_P_LO_Trip_SP + k_PZR_P_LO_Pretrip_Margin.

The trip setpoint h_PZR_P_LO_Trip_SP shall be k_PZR_P_LO_SP_Max at start-up. A pushbutton held or stuck in the pressed state (including at start-up) shall produce no reduction, an actuation made while f_PZR_P is invalid shall be ignored, and the setpoint shall hold its value while f_PZR_P is invalid. The Low Pressurizer Pressure trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_PZR_P_LO_OB_Ini) while f_PZR_P < k_PZR_P_LO_OB_Perm.

The RPS shall generate a Low Steam Generator 1 Water Level trip when the steam generator 1 water level (narrow range) (f_SG1_L) falls to or below k_SG1_L_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below k_SG1_L_LO_Pretrip_SP.

The trip setpoint h_SG2_P_LO_Trip_SP shall be k_SG2_P_LO_SP_Max at start-up.  Each operator actuation of the setpoint reset pushbutton f_SG2_P_LO_SP_Reset shall lower the setpoint to f_SG2_P - k_SG2_P_LO_Band, but not below k_SG2_P_LO_SP_Min; a reset shall never raise the setpoint and one actuation shall produce at most one reduction. The setpoint shall rise automatically so that it is never more than k_SG2_P_LO_Band below f_SG2_P, up to k_SG2_P_LO_SP_Max.
